the buckling of a cylindrical shell with two thin layers of different materials can be predicted by a fourth order obstacle problem with a constraint on the real-line, and that the solution of this problem can be approximated by an asymptotic series.

the buckling of two-layer shells is universal in the sense that it can be described using the same universal scaling constants for any material combination, and that the buckling load is determined by the elastic properties of the inner shell and the thickness of the outer shell.
